findings.explanation: high confidence.  Witness: The deduction that $Y = T$ for all $Y$ and the resulting equality $F_T = 2F_T$ is mathematically invalid. First, the presence of a term $F_T$ on the right-hand side of equation (3.2)/(p12-11) does not imply that every extension module $Y$ must be isomorphic to $T$. Second, even if $F_T$ and the other $F_Y$ were linearly independent, it would only imply that the coefficient of any other $F_Y$ must vanish, leaving $\chi(\mathbb{P}\mathrm{Ext}^1(M_1, M_2)) F_T = (\chi(\mathbb{P}\mathrm{Ext}^1(M_1, M_2)_T) + \chi(\mathbb{P}\mathrm{Ext}^1(M_2, M_1)_T)) F_T$, which does not yield $F_T = 2F_T$. Furthermore, an extension $T$ in $\mathrm{Ext}^1(M_1, M_2)$ does not simultaneously parameterize all of $\mathbb{P}\mathrm{Ext}^1(M_1, M_2)$ and $\mathbb{P}\mathrm{Ext}^1(M_2, M_1)$. Thus, deriving the contradiction $F_T = 2F_T$ is entirely baseless and invalidates the proof of Proposition 4.3 (and the subsequent results relying on it). Consequently, the claim of the paper is false/unsupported as written here.

Witness: Ext_A^1(M_1, M_2) \cong D Ext_A^1(M_2, M_1) only holds when M_1, M_2 correspond to modules locally free over \Pi(l) (Proposition 2.1), but fails for arbitrary modules over A = \mathbb{C}\Gamma^-/J (e.g. simple A-modules between which arrows in \Gamma^- are not bidirectional). Theorem 3.2 erroneously assumes this duality for all A-modules without the local freeness hypothesis from Proposition 2.1 / [GLS17, Theorem 1.8]. As a result, (3.2) is false for general A-modules, and the proof of Theorem 3.2 fails in general.
